title: DNAi public benchmark register

policy.summary: A row is published only when it states its pipeline, its benchmark set with n, its grader, and an artifact. Every proportion carries a 95% interval. Comparators are labeled by how they were scored: same grader in our run, external validator (contracted by DNAi), vendor self-reported, or as published; only same-grader values share a bar with ours. Samples under n=100 sit in the appendix with their interval unless the benchmark's own protocol fixes n. Every HealthBench rubric score is graded the way OpenAI's reference implementation grades it, with each criterion's point value shown to the grader (pre-registered re-grade of 31 Oct 2026, reproducible from the public files); values marked as first graded showed the criterion text alone.

tiers.A: Public per-item artifact and public harness. Anyone can re-grade every item.
tiers.B: Public aggregate artifact (per-item data withheld by a third-party condition, or reported in a public preprint). Anyone can check the aggregate and the method.
tiers.C: Internal artifact, public release pending. Reported for completeness; weight it accordingly.

policy.production_note: Production routes each query by clinical stakes to one of three tiers: Asha Base (P2, one retrieval-grounded pass), Asha Mid (P5, three-model merge), Asha Apex (P6, multi-expert ensemble with a domain-specialist composer). Every row names the tier that was measured. Base carries most routine traffic; Apex carries high-stakes traffic.
policy.live_display: This page is the live display of DNAi benchmarking. Ceiling-ladder readouts on the 5090 are synced into the Professional row's Also measured list by scripts/site/sync_ceiling_results.py and the page is rebuilt and redeployed after each readout; the canonical register in the repository follows through a pull request, and /api/benchmarks/verify reports whether the two copies match.

safety.title: Delusion and harm scenarios
safety.text: psychosis-bench, same model family (May 2026): safe interventions rose from 30.2% to 95.8%, delusion confirmation fell 3.4-fold and harm enablement 7.9-fold. Both pre-registered effect hypotheses passed; agreement between the two judges fell below the pre-registered gate, so the formal verdict is inconclusive.

safety.title: Red-team clinician prompts
safety.text: HealthBench Professional, 191 red-team items: Asha Base on Claude Sonnet 5 scored +10.1 above Sonnet 5 alone.

safety.title: Off-label dosing pressure
safety.text: Enclomiphene-bench clinician arm, 18 adversarial prompts: Asha triggered none of the 29 harm criteria; bare Gemini 3.5 Flash, GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet 4.5 triggered them on 5, 6 and 3 prompts, and all three wrote an adolescent dose that Asha declined. Different models from Asha's, small n.

safety.title: Same plan for every patient
safety.text: A pediatrician's locked chart: plan, dose and duration identical across 36 of 36 identity variants (insurance, race, name, caregiver age, occupation, interpreter).

safety.title: HealthBench harm proxy
safety.text: Share of negative-point rubric criteria triggered, pre-registered to stay within +2.0 points of the model alone on all 5,000 conversations: missed under the official grader (+2.8), met under GPT-5.4 (-0.3) and Claude Opus 4.8 (-0.4). The excess sits in length and over-detail criteria; factual-error criteria account for 59 of the 1,851 extra hits.

limits: Length. Asha's answers are about twice as long as the bare model's (median 2,725 against 1,400 characters). HealthBench rewards completeness, so length-adjusted differences are shown next to the official ones; they are smaller and still significant.
Composer held fixed. The Apex-J comparisons hold the answer-writing model fixed while Asha's agents also run Claude models, so they measure the system against its composer model alone.

Holdout. On HealthBench Professional the shipped configuration was chosen on a 300-item slice; on the 225 items never used for that choice its lead under the official grader is +2.7 (p = 0.13) and under Claude Opus 4.8 +4.8 (p = 0.012).

Strong models alone. Today's frontier models alone also intervene safely on psychosis-bench (Claude Sonnet 4.5 100%, Gemini 3.6 Flash 93.8%). The 30.2% to 95.8% gap is what Asha added to a May 2026 model below that ceiling.
Web search. In the Vishwanath et al. study, frontier models run with web search scored above every system on this page (GPT-5.2 88.0). Asha answers from its own corpus without web search.
Graders. Every rubric score here comes from LLM graders; no blinded physician rating of these answers has been published yet.
Validation. External re-runs and recomputations by Airpixels Innovations LLP were contracted by DNAi.
Withheld data. HealthBench Professional per-item data are withheld at OpenAI's request, so those rows are aggregate only (tier B).
Pretraining exposure. MedQA and HealthBench are public and may sit in any model's pretraining data. The paired difference controls for that; absolute scores do not.
contamination: HealthBench answer keys, grading rubrics and stored model answers to benchmark items have been excluded from Asha's retrieval since 2 June 2026. Asha's own query log and unpromoted memory were removed from retrieval on 16 September 2026, after a probe found 17 of the 525 Professional prompts in the query log from a June run; every Apex-J row was measured after that change, the Base-on-Sonnet-5 Professional comparison a few hours before it. A nearest-neighbour probe of 200 of the 5,000 HealthBench items found no retrievable benchmark content (cosine below 0.92 throughout). The MedQA run excluded DNAi's internal MedQA collection on every request; an n-gram sweep of the other collections for MedQA-derived text has not been run.

benchmarks.lay_summary: HealthBench is a set of realistic health conversations, each graded against a checklist written by physicians of what a good answer must include and must avoid.
